title: Decentralised Identifier-Anchored Verifiable Credentials with On-Chain Revocation for Social Media Identity Management
description: Reference implementation of an Ethereum registry of DID documents with per-credential revocation keyed by the issuer DID (Solidity), a Node.js service that issues W3C Verifiable Credentials with eddsa-jcs-2022 proofs (Ed25519, Multikey), a verifier that checks a credential against the registry with all reads pinned to one block, and the scripts, logs and tools behind the paper's measurements. Version 1.1.0: a pause no longer blocks revocation or deactivation; revocations carry an RFC 5280 reason code; administrator actions emit events; a controller handover needs the new address's acceptance; the registry stores no copies, which lowers the gas of revocation and DID creation; validFrom is checked; proofs follow eddsa-jcs-2022 section 3.3 and reproduce the W3C test vector; gas is reported for the osaka schedule and for the schedule Sepolia has used since 6 October 2026; 164 tests. The measurement code was frozen at commit 73b4cca16e7c before the Sepolia run of 12 November 2026. Added after the run, without changing that code: the timed local log of 9 November 2026; the closed Sepolia log of 12 November 2026; the v1.1.0 deployment record (contract 0x625eD772F70199BAc1A33A3BAF49B7394bBb5FC2 on Sepolia); the output of the unchanged earlier test and the log of the revised harness on the earlier code; the run-day rules (the pre-registration addendum and the run tools) with the manifest lines of the published files; the run checker and its tests; the final verdict and the analysis output; a sanitised summary of the network monitor; the figure scripts; and the transcript of the test run at the archived commit. The raw monitor and wrapper logs remain with the authors.
